reasons: CS4262 requires CS2106 (or CG2271) and (CS3244 or CS3264 or CG3201). CS4262 is fixed in Sem 4. CS2106 requires CS2100 (completed). CS3264 requires CS2109S and CS2040S (completed) and MA1522 (completed) and (EE2012A/EE2012/ST2131/MA2116/MA2116T/ST2334/MA2216). The student has ST2334. So CS3264 is eligible in Sem 4. However, CS4262 also requires CS2106. CS2106 is eligible in Sem 4. So Sem 4 can have CS2106, CS3264, CS4262. But wait, CS4262 prerequisite is (CS2106 or CG2271) AND (CS3244 or CS3264 or CG3201). If we take CS3264 in Sem 4, its prerequisite CS2109S must be completed or co-requisite. CS2109S is a must-take. If CS2109S is taken in Sem 4, it is a corequisite for CS3264? No, CS3264 prerequisite is CS2109S. Corequisites are not listed for CS3264, only prerequisites. So CS2109S must be completed before Sem 4 or taken as corequisite? The rule says 'Prerequisites must be completed or planned in a STRICTLY earlier semester. Corequisites in the same or an earlier semester.' CS2109S is a prerequisite for CS3264. So CS2109S must be in Sem 3 or earlier. The student is in Y2S2 (Sem 4). They have not completed CS2109S. They must take it. If they take it in Sem 4, it is not strictly earlier than Sem 4. So CS3264 cannot be taken in Sem 4 if CS2109S is taken in Sem 4. CS2109S must be taken in Sem 3. But the student is currently in Sem 4. They cannot go back to Sem 3. Thus, CS2109S is not completed before Sem 4. Therefore, CS3264 cannot be taken in Sem 4. CS4262 requires CS3264 (or CS3244/CG3201). CS3244 requires EE2211 or EE2213. Neither is completed. CS3244 cannot be taken in Sem 4 without prereqs. CG3201 requires EE2211 or EE2213. Neither is completed. So CS4262 cannot be taken in Sem 4 because its second part of the AND condition cannot be met with completed courses or courses taken in Sem 4 (since their prereqs are not met). Specifically, CS3264 needs CS2109S completed before. CS2109S is not completed. CS3244 needs EE2211/EE2213. CG3201 needs EE2211/EE2213. None of these are completed. So CS4262 is impossible in Sem 4.
